$comment: Popular websites' own keyboard shortcuts in the Ctrl/Cmd+Shift, Ctrl/Cmd+Alt, Shift+Alt and Ctrl/Cmd+Alt+Shift families, so an app can tell when its hotkey would collide with the page it runs on. Companion to docs/site-hotkeys.md (generated from this file) and the research notes in docs/site-hotkeys/. Unlike data/browser-hotkeys.json (browser/OS keys that never reach the page), these keys DO reach the page and the site handles them; the app decides whether to yield.

version.method: Vendor help pages and keymap source, read by research agents (often through a summarizing fetch). verified=true means read on the vendor page or source in that session; false means a secondary source or inference. Sites the agents could not read have researched=false and no rows.

$keyFormat: Same as data/browser-hotkeys.json: lowercase, modifiers in canonical order ctrl, meta, alt, shift, then the key (letters, digits, period, comma, semicolon, quote, slash, backslash, bracketleft, bracketright, minus, equal, backquote, enter, space, tab, arrows, home, end, pageup, pagedown, f1..f12). Physical keys: Ctrl+> is ctrl+shift+period. Per platform: windows (also used for linux), mac (meta = Cmd, alt = Option, ctrl = Control), chromeos.
$hostFormat: hosts: exact hostnames, "*.example.com" for any subdomain, or "*" for any host (then pathPrefixes narrow it). hostsConfirmed=false means the hostnames were inferred, not observed.
